transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-10
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Atlas Eng Mgr), Carlos Reyes (Atlas ML Eng), Sanjay Patel (Atlas Head of AI)

[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the weekly POC sync. Quick roll call, we got Maya and Liam from Redwood, and Priya, Carlos, Sanjay on the Atlas side, correct?
[00:00:08] Priya: Yep that's right, thanks Maya.
[00:00:10] Sanjay: Morning all.
[00:00:12] Maya: Cool. Agenda — quick run through the small benchmark results you sent, talk model candidates for pinning, discuss rollback/fallback options, and agree next steps. Does that sound good?
[00:00:21] Carlos: Yeah looks good. We also had a couple security questions but we can touch that at the end.
[00:00:26] Liam: Great. Quick note — transcription may mess up some model names, folks, so apologies in advance, my accent and the automation sometimes collude.

[00:01:02] -- Summary of Atlas's preliminary results --
[00:01:05] Priya: We ran the small 200 prompt pass on staging last week. The gist — rwd-13b-qtz-8 is cheapest but 95th pct latency was 420ms for short prompts and spiked to 1.3s for longer context. The redwood-rtx-7b-v2 family had much better tail latency (~220ms 95th) but cost per token is higher.
[00:01:30] Carlos: Yeah, and we saw the Llama2-13b baseline produce slightly higher token counts so cost wound up a bit worse than expected. Also our kv cache warming pattern is different in staging vs prod, so numbers might shift.
[00:01:48] Liam: Got it, thanks. Couple of clarifications — when you say spike to 1.3s, is that cold-start or steady-state with batching?
[00:01:55] Carlos: Mostly steady-state with 32-sample batching off; it's more about long-context window decode time, so it's not purely cold-start.
[00:02:03] Liam: Okay, that helps. Sounds like there's a sweet spot with the 7b variant for tail latency.

[00:03:10] -- Model catalog and pinning discussion --
[00:03:13] Maya: For pinning, our recommendation is to pick one primary model per route and a compatible fallback. Example: primary = redwood-rtx-7b-v2 (pinned to v2.1), fallback = rwd-13b-qtz-8-compat for cost-sensitive bursts, and a cheaper quantized variant for degraded mode.
[00:03:31] Sanjay: When you say "pinned to v2.1" — what does that pin include? Kernel selection? Quantization?
[00:03:36] Liam: Good question. Pinning means we fix the model artifact and the inference config: model weights identifier, quantization profile, and runtime optimization flags. It doesn't lock the infra instance type; you can still scale nodes.
[00:03:48] Priya: Are there compatibility guarantees if we fallback to a different architecture? e.g., from rtx-7b to rwd-13b-qtz-8 — will responses be meaningfully different?
[00:03:57] Liam: They will differ — semantics and tokenization can shift. For user-facing features you should evaluate quality regressions with a short eval set. We usually recommend a small golden prompt set to measure key metrics before accepting a fallback as safe.
[00:04:10] Carlos: We have that golden set from our eval team — we'll run that against the candidates.

[00:05:20] -- Rollback and automatic fallback strategies --
[00:05:23] Maya: Operationally, we provide several options: immediate atomic rollback to previous pinned model, or a staged canary with automatic rollback on quality or latency regression. There's also automatic fallback routing policy — route to fallback model when queue wait exceeds threshold or per-tenant policy.
[00:05:40] Carlos: For canaries, do you support traffic split by percentage and automatic rollbacks based on 95th pct latency and token error rate?
[00:05:48] Liam: Yes, you can split traffic (e.g., 5% canary) and set SLO triggers. We support metric-based rollback (latency, error rates) and score-based rollback if you send back a small eval metric payload.
[00:06:00] Priya: What about stateful contexts — KV cache — won't switching models break continuations?
[00:06:07] Liam: Correct — KV cache is model-specific. For rolling between different architectures we recommend session-level affinity: you either pin session to model family or accept a warm restart. For chat continuity we recommend only switching within compatible families.

[00:07:30] -- Cost vs latency tradeoff discussion --
[00:07:33] Sanjay: From our product POV, 95th pct latency is more important than minimal cost. We can tolerate some cost if it keeps tail stable.
[00:07:40] Maya: That lines up with the data. The 7b family hits your 95th SLO in our tests more reliably. We can optimize cost by selective fallback for non-latency-critical routes.
[00:07:49] Carlos: We have some churn-heavy routes (summarization logs) where cheaper fallback makes sense.

[00:08:45] -- Benchmarks and larger-run plan --
[00:08:47] Liam: Next recommended step — run a 1k prompt run with production-like arrival patterns (bursty, mixed lengths). That will surface queuing behavior and real tail. We'll provide a benchmark spreadsheet to collect the results and add columns for token counts, p50/p95/p99, and memory/CPU footprint.
[00:09:00] Maya: We'll send an initial pinned set we think makes sense: redwood-rtx-7b-v2.1 (primary), rwd-13b-qtz-8-compat (fallback), and rtx-7b-qtz-4 for degraded cheap mode.
[00:09:12] Priya: Sounds good — please include explicit model IDs so we can pin in the atlas dev account.

[00:10:40] -- Security and private deployment questions --
[00:10:43] Priya: Quick security Qs: if we go private, does the call to KMS + HSM differ for pinning? We need to show auditors exact encryption flow.
[00:10:51] Maya: Private deployment will let you manage KMS keys; model artifact locks can be configured to require KMS signing. We'll send the KMS/HSM snippet and SOC2 summary in the security pack.
[00:11:00] Sanjay: Also need to know audit log retention for inference requests and token-level billing traces.
[00:11:05] Liam: We capture token-level billing and you can configure retention up to enterprise plan limits. For private, logs can be routed to your S3 and we support immutable audit append if needed.

[00:12:22] -- Edge cases and gotchas --
[00:12:25] Carlos: One thing we saw — when we tried the quantized variant, the tokenizer sometimes produced slightly different subword splits, causing downstream regex-based parsers to fail. Any guidance?
[00:12:34] Liam: That's a known subtlety. Two mitigations — normalize tokenization in your downstream parser or pick a fallback that's tokenizer-compatible. We can run a tokenization diff report for your golden prompts.
[00:12:44] Priya: That would be helpful.

[00:13:50] -- Live Q&A and clarifications --
[00:13:53] Sanjay: If we pin to a model but Redwood publishes a security patch for the runtime, will we automatically get the patch or is that a manual opt-in?
[00:14:00] Maya: Security patches to the runtime are pushed automatically at infra layer; model artifact pin prevents weight changes. We separate runtime updates from model artifact changes.
[00:14:10] Carlos: Nice. One more — is there a way to do canary only on certain tenants (we have VIP customers)?
[00:14:18] Liam: Yes, routing policies can be per-tenant, per-route, or global. You can carve out VIP tenants to never fallback or to always use primaries.

[00:15:40] -- Short demo of pin config (Liam) --
[00:15:43] Liam: (screen share narration) Here is the policy YAML — model_id: redwood-rtx-7b-v2.1, pinned: true, fallback: rwd-13b-qtz-8-compat, rollback_on: [p95>500ms, error_rate>0.5%], canary: 5%.
[00:16:01] Priya: YAML looks good. We may want rollback_on to include a quality threshold based on eval score.
[00:16:06] Liam: Yup you can send a small eval payload via the eval endpoint and set score-drop triggers.

[00:17:30] -- Minor transcription artifacts / misc --
[00:17:33] Maya: Note — Fireflies sometimes shows "k-v cash" instead of KV cache in exports, ignore that.
[00:17:39] Carlos: Haha noted.

[00:18:55] -- Decision points and alignment --
[00:18:58] Maya: To recap decisions from this call: Atlas will run the 1k benchmark; Redwood will propose pinned model IDs and provide the benchmark sheet + security pack; routing policy will be set to primary=rtx-7b-v2.1, fallback=13b-qtz-8-compatible for non-VIP routes.
[00:19:13] Priya: Agreed. Also we'll share the golden eval set for quality checks.

[00:20:45] -- Scheduling and next sync --
[00:20:48] Maya: Let's plan to reconvene after the 1k run — propose next Wednesday 2025-02-19 same time, unless you want earlier.
[00:20:55] Priya: That works.

[00:21:40] -- Closing clarifications --
[00:21:42] Carlos: One operational ask — can Redwood provide example infra sizing for the pinned models (GPU/CPU footprint) so we can provision staging appropriately?
[00:21:51] Liam: We'll add a sizing table to the spreadsheet with recommended instance types and memory.
[00:21:56] Sanjay: Great.

[00:22:10] Maya: Alright thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts. Ending early given we covered the agenda.
[00:22:16] Priya: Thanks all.
[00:22:18] Sanjay: Thanks.

(Transcript note: occasional transcription errors present; some product names may be slightly altered e.g., rwd vs redwood abbreviations.)
